questions.question:
Select the most appropriate homophone to fill in the blank.

Ruby gave her mother a hug and offered to knead the _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**flour**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "flour" refers to a powder obtained by grinding grain, typically wheat, and used to make bread, cakes, and pastry. (आटा)
 
• Kneading is a process typically associated with making dough, which is made from flour.
 
• The other options: "flora," "flavour," and "floor" do not fit the context of kneading.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *Ruby gave her mother a hug and offered to knead the flour__.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

• **Flavour (स्वाद)**: The distinctive taste of a food or drink.
 
• **Floor (मंजिल)**: The lower surface of a room, on which one may walk.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The line, 'Round the rugged rocks the ragged rascal ran' uses the repetition of usually initial consonant sounds in two or __more neighbouring words or syllables .__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. alliteration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"alliteration"** means the repetition of usually initial consonant sounds in two or more neighboring words or syllables. (अनुप्रास)

 
 
• **Example: **Sally sells sea shells by the sea shore.
 
 
 
• **"Epithet"** refers to a descriptive term or phrase expressing a quality or characteristic of the person or thing mentioned. (विशेषण)
 
 
• **Example: **Alexander the Great.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the use of initial consonant sounds repetitively is called **'alliteration'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. alliteration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Epithet** (विशेषण): A descriptive term or phrase expressing a quality or characteristic of the person or thing mentioned.

 
 
• **Example:** He earned the epithet "Alexander the Great" for his conquests.
 
 
 
• **Simile** (उपमा): A figure of speech involving the comparison of one thing with another thing of a different kind, used to make a description more emphatic or vivid.
 
 
• **Example:** As brave as a lion.
 
 
 
• **Allegory** (रूपक): A narrative in which characters and events represent abstract ideas or concepts.
 
 
• **Example:** George Orwell's "Animal Farm" is an allegory of the Russian Revolution.

options.text: my friend calls me and ask

questions.solution:

• The sentence begins in the past tense ("While I was walking"), so the rest of the sentence should also be consistent in tense.
 
• The phrase "my friend calls me" should be in the past tense to match the first part of the sentence. It should be "my friend called me."

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

We should clean the house regularly.

options.text: The house should have been cleaned regularly by us.
The house should be being cleaned regularly by us.
The house should be cleaned regularly by us.
The house should be clean regularly by us.

questions.solution:
```html
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "We should clean the house regularly."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "the house" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "should clean" to "should be cleaned" (modal + be + past participle).
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "us."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The house should be cleaned regularly by us."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"The house should have been cleaned regularly by us." – Incorrect tense (past perfect modal passive).
 
• **Option 2: **"The house should be being cleaned regularly by us." – Incorrect use of present continuous passive.
 
• **Option 4: **"The house should be clean regularly by us." – Incorrect verb form (clean instead of cleaned).

``

questions.question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the parts in the correct sequence to

form a meaningful sentence.

(P) hard work and perseverance

(Q) no matter how difficult

(O) lead to success

(R) the journey may seem
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The main subject of the sentence should come first, followed by the result.
 
• **Part P is the first** because it introduces the main subject, "hard work and perseverance":
 
 
• "hard work and perseverance"
 
 
 
• **Part O follows next** to link with the result, "lead to success":
 
 
• "lead to success"
 
 
 
• **Part Q is the third** introducing the condition, "no matter how difficult":
 
 
• "no matter how difficult"
 
 
 
• **Part R comes last** to add detail to the condition, "the journey may seem":
 
 
• "the journey may seem"
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **POQR**.

 

**Coherent sentence after rearrangement**:

"Hard work and perseverance lead to success no matter how difficult the journey may seem."

questions.question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the sentences in the correct

order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Summative assessment is the assignment of the student’s performance at the end of the academic term.

B. This new pattern ensures that besides just textbook teaching and learning, effective child-teacher interaction is

encouraged.

C. The CBSE envisages two types of examinations, Formative and Summative.

D. Formative assessment is a part of the teaching-learning process and is done through conversation, quizzes, interviews,

projects, assignments, etc.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Part C should come first** as it introduces the overall topic of CBSE examinations:

 
 
• "The CBSE envisages two types of examinations, Formative and Summative."
 
 
 
• **Part D follows next** as it provides details about Formative assessment:
 
 
• "Formative assessment is a part of the teaching-learning process and is done through conversation, quizzes, interviews, projects, assignments, etc."
 
 
 
• **Part A then explains Summative assessment**:
 
 
• "Summative assessment is the assignment of the student’s performance at the end of the academic term."
 
 
 
• **Part B concludes** by discussing how the new pattern affects the teaching and learning process:
 
 
• "This new pattern ensures that besides just textbook teaching and learning, effective child-teacher interaction is encouraged."
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **C, D, A, B**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"The CBSE envisages two types of examinations, Formative and Summative. Formative assessment is a part of the teaching-learning process and is done through conversation, quizzes, interviews, projects, assignments, etc. Summative assessment is the assignment of the student’s performance at the end of the academic term. This new pattern ensures that besides just textbook teaching and learning, effective child-teacher interaction is encouraged."

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

His father's arm was bandaged by the kind nurse.

options.text: The kind nurse has bandaged his father's arm.
The kind nurse had bandaged his father's arm.
The kind nurse bandages his father's arm.
The kind nurse bandaged his father's arm.

questions.solution:
```html
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "The kind nurse bandaged his father's arm."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "his father's arm" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "bandaged" to "was bandaged" (past simple passive).
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "the kind nurse."
 
• Ensure the sentence structure remains clear.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The kind nurse bandaged his father's arm."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"The kind nurse has bandaged his father's arm." – Incorrect tense (present perfect).
 
• **Option 2: **"The kind nurse had bandaged his father's arm." – Incorrect tense (past perfect).
 
• **Option 3: **"The kind nurse bandages his father's arm." – Incorrect tense (present simple).

```

questions.question:
Read the sentence carefully and select the ANTONYM of the underlined word from the given options.

I heard his suggestion but I am quite __unsure __about the risks involved in it.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. 'Certain'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"unsure"** means not feeling, showing, or done with confidence and certainty; uncertain. (अशांत या अनिश्चित)

 
 
• **Example: **She felt unsure about her decision to move to a new city.
 
 
 
• **"Certain"** refers to being completely confident or having no doubt about something. (निश्चित या विश्वासपूर्ण)
 
 
• **Example: **He was certain that he locked the door before leaving the house.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'unsure'** is **'certain'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. 'Certain'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Thoughtful **(विचारशील): Showing consideration or care for others; reflective.

 
 
• **Example:** She gave a thoughtful speech that moved everyone in the audience.
 
 
 
• **Interested **(दिलचस्पी): Showing curiosity or concern about something.
 
 
• **Example: **He was very interested in learning about different cultures.
 
 
 
• **Doubtful** (संदेहास्पद): Feeling uncertain or lacking conviction.
 
 
• **Example:** She was doubtful about the success of the new project.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'that has'**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] ** __Key Points__ ** 

__
 
• The passage refers to a rise in global temperature, a singular noun, that has already occurred.
 
• The correct relative pronoun and verb form combination to match the singular antecedent "rise" is "**that has**".
 
• The other options do not match the subject-verb agreement correctly.

Therefore, the correct answer is **'that has'**.

 

Complete Passage: *The rise in global temperature ***that has**__* already occurred is leading to extreme weather events that bring *__**with them**__* heat waves and droughts, devastating floods and increasingly powerful hurricanes and tropical storms. The combination of these factors means the impact on human health is increasing and is *__**set to**__* accelerate. But there is room for hope, particularly if governments take action now to *__**honor**__* the pledges made at Glasgow in November 2021 and to go further in resolving the climate crisis. WHO is *__**urging**__* governments to lead a just, equitable, and fast phase out of fossil fuels and transition to a clean energy future.* 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] ** __Additional Information__ ** 

 
• **Which had:** Incorrect because it implies past perfect tense which is not suitable for the context.
 
• **That is:** Incorrect because it implies the temperature rise is currently happening rather than having already occurred.
 
• **Which have:** Incorrect because it implies a plural subject, while "rise" is singular.
 
• **That has:** Correct because it matches the singular antecedent "rise" and the present perfect tense needed for something that has already occurred.

• The phrase "extreme weather events" in the passage indicates that the temperature rise is causing severe and strong weather changes.
 
• The word "**intense**" accurately describes severe and strong weather conditions, fitting the context of heat waves and droughts.
 
• Other options like '**mild**', '**maximise**', and '**minor**' do not convey the required severity or intensity appropriate to the context.

Therefore, the correct answer is **'intense'**.

 

Complete Passage: *The rise in global temperature* **that has**__ *already occurred is leading to extreme weather events that bring* __**intense**__ *heat waves and droughts, devastating floods and increasingly powerful hurricanes and tropical storms. The combination of these factors means the impact on human health is increasing and is* __**set to**__ *accelerate. But there is room for hope, particularly if governments take action now to* __**honor**__ *the pledges made at Glasgow in November 2021 and to go further in resolving the climate crisis. WHO is* __**urging**__ *governments to lead a just, equitable, and fast phase out of fossil fuels and transition to a clean energy future.*

• Other options like '**calling at**', '**calling for**', and '**calling from**' do not fit this context correctly.

Therefore, the correct answer is **'calling on'**.
